en: We built our first amazing application that
arguably doesn't do much.
Now, what else can you build with Deno then?
The most prominent use case probably would
be web apps or websites.
Web apps are in the end just a fancy term
for saying websites.
Building web apps with Deno will probably be
the main
use case, the main scenario where you want
to use Deno.
You can build any kind of website with Deno,
that's important. You can build websites
where you render views on the server side
with templating engines and you can also
build APIs like REST or GraphQL APIs.
In case that doesn't tell you too much yet,
you will see what this is and what the
differences are throughout the course. These
are simply different kinds of web apps you
can build in the end.
So web apps and websites, that's the main
use case and you can really build anything
with Deno here.
You can also use it, however, to build any
kind of utility script or tool, because in
the end you can run JavaScript outside of
the browser. And as you will also see
throughout the course, Deno will be able to
interact with your file system to read and
write or delete files and all these kinds of
things. So therefore you can basically do
any kind of read/write operation on your
computer. You can write to a database, you
can do whatever you want. You can interact
with files or databases, and therefore you
can write any kind of script or program that
you want to execute locally. You could write
your own cleanup script, which basically
checks how long a file hasn't been used and
deletes it if it's been
unused for, let's say, 30 days. Something
like this would be possible with Deno.
By the way, you can build the exact same
things with Node.js.
So in case you don't know Node.js yet, you
can build the same things with Node.js. In
case you do know Node.js, You can build the
same things with Deno. Really, you can use
them interchangeably. Just the way you build
it and what's built into those runtimes and
technologies, that's what's different.
